tool-intro-text.text:
### 01 Card

Put one thought on a card. Use Markdown headings, lists and emphasis. Double-click to edit.

tool-detail-text.text:
### 01 Card — a closer look

#### How to use it
Place a card and double-click its body. Use headings, lists, emphasis and links. Properties controls font size, padding, corners, fill and border.

#### Keep in mind
Separate ideas or tasks, then use position and overlap to add meaning. Ask your AI to split a long passage into cards and clip them together.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-shapes.text:
### 02 Shapes

Give ideas a shape: rectangles, ellipses, diamonds and more. Add text, then change the fill and border.

tool-detail-shapes.text:
### 02 Shapes — a closer look

#### How to use it
Choose a shape, then double-click to add text. Adjust colors, lines and text fitting in Properties.

#### Keep in mind
Attach lines to anchors. Connections follow when the shape moves, making shapes useful for concepts and flowcharts.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-line.text:
### 03 Line

Connect two points. Attach ends to anchors so they follow cards and diagrams. Choose dashes, width and end markers.

tool-detail-line.text:
### 03 Line — a closer look

#### How to use it
Place a line and move its ends. Bring an end near an anchor to attach it; hold Alt to avoid snapping. Set border color, width, dashes and end markers.

#### Keep in mind
Join lines at junctions and round their corners. The Line dropdown also offers Connected lines and Freehand lines.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-arrow.text:
### 04 Arrow

Show direction or flow. Arrows share the same connections as lines, including junctions and rounded corners.

tool-detail-arrow.text:
### 04 Arrow — a closer look

#### How to use it
An arrow is a line with an arrowhead. Add or remove end markers later. Attached ends follow their targets.

#### Keep in mind
Arrowheads express a relationship, not travel restrictions. A wayfinder can follow the route in either direction.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-continuous.text:
### 05 Connected lines

Choose Connected lines from Line ▼. Click successive points, then finish with Enter or Esc. Edit or extend the result as ordinary lines.

tool-detail-continuous.text:
### 05 Connected lines — a closer look

#### How to use it
Choose Connected lines from Line ▼ and click each bend. Press Enter or Esc to finish. The result is a set of normal line objects.

#### Keep in mind
Connect to existing ends, hold Alt to avoid snapping, round junctions or undo. You can stop, adjust the lines and continue later.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-free-line.text:
### 06 Freehand lines

Drag a rough route from Line ▼. On release, it becomes a few straight segments. Use Doodle to keep your original strokes.

tool-detail-free-line.text:
### 06 Freehand lines — a closer look

#### How to use it
Choose Freehand lines from Line ▼ and drag. On release, the path is simplified into a few editable line segments.

#### Keep in mind
Useful for rough roads and concept maps. Use Doodle when you want to keep the movement and character of your handwriting.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-pin.text:
### 07 Pin

Numbered landmarks in a series. Attach pins to items and follow their thread with the previous and next buttons.

tool-detail-pin.text:
### 07 Pin — a closer look

#### How to use it
Place a pin to number it within its series. Create series and choose their colors, shapes and numbering. Attached pins follow movement and resizing.

#### Keep in mind
A series can show a connecting thread. Select a pin and use the previous or next button to travel in number order.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-wayfinder.text:
### 08 Wayfinder

Follow connected lines across the desk. Move moves quickly; Tour goes slowly. At a branch, choose a route on a small map.

tool-detail-wayfinder.text:
### 08 Wayfinder — a closer look

#### How to use it
Attach a wayfinder to a card, then connect one line at its top, left or right. Press its round play button. Place wayfinders at both ends to travel back and forth.

#### Keep in mind
Move accelerates and slows down; Tour moves at a steady pace. Choose a direction at branches. Click or use a key to stop along the route.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-clip.text:
### 09 Clip

Bundle cards and documents. Spread them by a fixed gap or a proportion, including edge-to-edge. Alt-drag to pull one sheet out.

tool-detail-clip.text:
### 09 Clip — a closer look

#### How to use it
Select items and clip them together. Attachment position and spacing determine their arrangement. Spacing can use a fixed distance, a percentage of the previous sheet, or the first sheet's short side.

#### Keep in mind
100% of the previous sheet places sheets edge-to-edge. Alt-drag a sheet to remove it. Delete the clip to release the bundle while keeping the contents.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-file.text:
### 10 Clear Folder

Keep several items together without changing their arrangement. Clips and rulers can go inside with their contents.

tool-detail-file.text:
### 10 Clear Folder — a closer look

#### How to use it
Select items and place them in a Clear Folder. Clip and ruler groups are included as a whole. Move the colored frame and title to carry the arrangement together.

#### Keep in mind
Individual movement, resizing and reordering are restricted inside. Release the folder to rearrange its contents. Deleting the folder leaves its contents in place.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-ruler.text:
### 11 Ruler

Arrange items along both long edges. Choose free placement, equal gaps or equal centers, with acrylic, bamboo or steel looks.

tool-detail-ruler.text:
### 11 Ruler — a closer look

#### How to use it
Place a ruler and arrange cards or documents along either long edge. Its orientation determines the alignment direction. Choose free placement, equal gaps or equal centers; each side is arranged separately.

#### Keep in mind
Choose acrylic, bamboo or stainless steel. Moving the ruler carries its items. A Clear Folder can contain the whole group.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-image-svg.text:
### 12 Image / SVG

Put photos and illustrations on the desk. Move or resize them, or use Open to view them in another tab.

tool-detail-image-svg.text:
### 12 Image / SVG — a closer look

#### How to use it
Use Image, drop a file or paste from the clipboard. Images and SVGs can have titles and can be moved or resized. Open them in another tab for a closer look.

#### Keep in mind
Your AI can read and revise SVG source. This is not a freehand editor for arbitrary SVGs; use Doodle for a drawing you want to keep editing by hand.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-doodle.text:
### 13 Doodle

Place a blank sheet, set its size and double-click to draw. Switch among three colors and three widths. A transparent sheet can overlay other material.

tool-detail-doodle.text:
### 13 Doodle — a closer look

#### How to use it
Place a Doodle, size its sheet and double-click. Add a title and reopen it later. Choose among three colors and three widths; each dropdown offers widths from 2 to 64. The eraser uses the same widths.

#### Keep in mind
Resizing changes the sheet while retaining strokes. Moving the drawing and panning the view are separate operations. The editor has its own Undo until you apply the drawing.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-cutout.text:
### 14 Cutout

Overlay a closed shape on an image and select both to show only that area. Keep the original and toggle the cutout off again.

tool-detail-cutout.text:
### 14 Cutout — a closer look

#### How to use it
Overlap a document with a closed shape and select both. Cutout copies the shape's outline as a mask; moving the original shape later does not change the mask.

#### Keep in mind
The original data remains. Toggle Cutout off to see it all. Each item has one mask, replaced by a new cutout. Copy the visible result as an image for other apps.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-mermaid.text:
### 15 Mermaid

Draw a diagram from text. Edit the source to change its structure. Even if rendering fails, the source remains.

tool-detail-mermaid.text:
### 15 Mermaid — a closer look

#### How to use it
Write Mermaid source to generate a diagram of steps, relationships or structure. If rendering fails, correct the retained source and generate it again.

#### Keep in mind
The diagram is one document, not a set of separate shapes. Connect pins or lines to its outer frame and organize it with clips or rulers. Your AI can help edit the source.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-qr.text:
### 16 QR code

Send text or a URL to a phone. The source text is retained. Adjust the outer frame while the QR code stays square.

tool-detail-qr.text:
### 16 QR code — a closer look

#### How to use it
Enter text or a URL. Spaces and line breaks are retained. Resizing the frame keeps the QR square. Enlarge it if it becomes too small to scan.

#### Keep in mind
Content is not split automatically. If it exceeds capacity, a Too long sign appears and the source stays intact. Stickers reserve a row of space above and below.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-web.text:
### 17 Web page

Keep a web reference beside your ideas and documents. Open the original page when you need it.

tool-detail-web.text:
### 17 Web page — a closer look

#### How to use it
Place a web page card with a URL. View it alongside your material or use its Open button to visit the original page.

#### Keep in mind
Embedding restrictions or network conditions may prevent display on the desk. Open the original in your browser instead. This tool does not guarantee an offline copy.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-link.text:
### 18 Link

A doorway to a URL. Switch between URL text and a QR code. Use the Open button to visit the page.

tool-detail-link.text:
### 18 Link — a closer look

#### How to use it
Set a title and URL. Choose URL text or QR code display in Properties. In text mode, adjust font, color, corners, fill and border. The chain icon identifies a link.

#### Keep in mind
The text, QR and Open button all use the same URL. QR mode ignores frame decoration. Use QR code instead for arbitrary text that is not a URL.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-desk-link.text:
### 19 Desk link

A card pointing to another saved desk. Look for the desk icon and use its Open button to switch.

tool-detail-desk-link.text:
### 19 Desk link — a closer look

#### How to use it
This special link refers to a desk file on the connected server, rather than an ordinary web page. Use its Open button to switch desks.

#### Keep in mind
If the current desk has changes, choose to save, discard or cancel. Moved files, deleted files and different paths on another computer are not tracked automatically.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-paste.text:
### 20 Paste

Add text, images or SVGs from the clipboard. Copy editable items between desks connected to the same MCP server.

tool-detail-paste.text:
### 20 Paste — a closer look

#### How to use it
Paste text, images or SVGs. If copied desk-object data is available, items are restored as editable objects. Other desks on the same MCP server can exchange these copies.

#### Keep in mind
If object data is unavailable, clipboard text or an image is used instead. Internal object copies and image/text copies for other apps serve different purposes.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-stamp.text:
### 21 Stamp

Mark something completed, on hold, approved or simply worth a comment. Hover for a large preview and add a date if you like.

tool-detail-stamp.text:
### 21 Stamp — a closer look

#### How to use it
Select cards or a Clear Folder, then choose from 38 stamps. Hover over a small stamp to preview it. The large preview is clickable too. Add date sits below it and is remembered in this browser.

#### Keep in mind
Stamps are visual marks: they do not change the text or task state. They retreat to a corner while selected, apart from the brief pressing effect. Clear removes the stamp. Japanese lettering is part of the design; the English UI explains its meaning.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-reaction.text:
### 22 Reaction

Add a feeling, reply or small flag with an emoji. Mark a question or a check without editing the body.

tool-detail-reaction.text:
### 22 Reaction — a closer look

#### How to use it
Add or remove several kinds of reaction. In Properties, set their size, corner, direction and Fixed zoom. Bars and moon phases can also serve as informal progress flags.

#### Keep in mind
Reactions, stamps and stickers have no mandatory workflow meaning. Use reactions for feelings or small flags, stamps for a prominent mark, and stickers for colors or counts.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-sticker.text:
### 23 Sticker

Choose a color and shape, then stick on small marks in order. Use them for categories or ratings; they arrange themselves from a corner.

tool-detail-sticker.text:
### 23 Sticker — a closer look

#### How to use it
Open the Sticker dropdown: choose Shape, Suggested colors or All colors. Choices stay open so you can set them together. Press the main button to add the current sticker. Use strips 1 and 2 independently.

#### Keep in mind
Set the shared diameter, corner and Fixed zoom in Properties. Stickers wrap as needed. Clear a strip and reapply to change its order. They follow the parent item and their settings can be copied with the format eyedropper.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-prop.text:
### 24 Props

Tea cups, signs and a temporary area. With Select by header enabled, grab the top band and work with the cards inside.

tool-detail-prop.text:
### 24 Props — a closer look

#### How to use it
Place SVG props such as cups, signs and areas. Move or resize them like other items. VACANT LOT, WORK IN PROGRESS and TEMP AREA are separate English designs; the Japanese designs remain available.

#### Keep in mind
Select by header makes just the top band selectable so you can work with cards inside. Resizing is disabled in that mode; turn it off to resize again. Decorative props do not perform the actions they depict.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-format.text:
### 25 Pick / Apply format

Pick a sample's appearance and apply it to selected items. Keep the current format and three saved presets.

tool-detail-format.text:
### 25 Pick / Apply format — a closer look

#### How to use it
Use Pick format on a sample, select the target, then Apply. Keep frequently used appearances in the current slot and three saved presets.

#### Keep in mind
Only supported style properties are applied; text and position stay unchanged. Sticker and reaction settings are included. Selecting an item alone does not replace the saved sample.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

guide-sample-object-pin-format.description: Pick / Apply format: Try the example

tool-intro-callout.text:
### 26 Callout

Add a speech, thought or line tail to a card. Attach its tip to show what your note is about.

tool-detail-callout.text:
### 26 Callout — a closer look

#### How to use it
Choose a tail in the card's Properties: a triangle, thought dots or an elbow line. Move its tip and optionally attach it to an anchor.

#### Keep in mind
The body holds the note; the tip points to its subject. An attached tip follows its target. Remove the tail to make it an ordinary card again.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-preview.text:
### 27 Markdown preview

While editing, hold Preview to check uncommitted text. Previewing does not change the saved card body.

tool-detail-preview.text:
### 27 Markdown preview — a closer look

#### How to use it
Open a card for editing and hold Preview to see its current Markdown. Check headings, line breaks and formatting before applying.

#### Keep in mind
Return to the input and keep editing. Preview alone does not apply the text. For substantial writing, you can also copy from an external text editor.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-selection.text:
### 28 Selection

Click to select, drag to move. Add items with Shift or Ctrl, or drag a selection box to handle several at once.

tool-detail-selection.text:
### 28 Selection — a closer look

#### How to use it
Click one item or select several with a box. Shift or Ctrl adds to the selection. Drag the selection to move it. Resize using edge or corner handles where supported.

#### Keep in mind
Human selection drives Properties and editing. AI pointing is a separate attention frame. Arrow keys move selected items; Shift plus arrows resize them, and Alt temporarily bypasses snapping.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-pointing.text:
### 29 AI pointing

A separate frame shows what your AI is referring to. Clear AI pointing removes it without changing your selection.

tool-detail-pointing.text:
### 29 AI pointing — a closer look

#### How to use it
Your AI can point to an item without changing your selection. It is a shared reference for phrases such as this card. Use Clear AI pointing to remove the frame.

#### Keep in mind
When your AI points and then moves an item, the animation makes it easier to follow. Pointing does not lock the object or change its saved content. Try it in the connected edition.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-snap.text:
### 30 Snap

Align placement to a grid. Turn it on for tidy rows, or off for free placement.

tool-detail-snap.text:
### 30 Snap — a closer look

#### How to use it
Turn Snap on to align placement. In Desk appearance, set Grid interval and Snap interval. A 4:1 ratio gives four snapping steps per visible grid interval.

#### Keep in mind
Use it for diagrams or rows, then switch it off or hold Alt for fine placement. Endpoint snapping to anchors is a separate aid. AI operations can also request exact coordinates.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-lock.text:
### 31 Lock

Prevent accidental mouse movement and resizing. Text, styling and AI operations can still be changed.

tool-detail-lock.text:
### 31 Lock — a closer look

#### How to use it
Lock an item to protect its position and size from mouse gestures. Group membership in clips and folders can also affect what can move.

#### Keep in mind
Lock is not a permission or secrecy setting. It does not prohibit every edit or AI operation. Use it to hold a layout in place.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-layers.text:
### 32 Front / Back

Change what overlaps what. Bring a note forward or send a background behind other items.

tool-detail-layers.text:
### 32 Front / Back — a closer look

#### How to use it
Select an item and use Front or Back to change its stacking order. Put notes over documents or place background items behind them.

#### Keep in mind
Clips, Clear Folders and rulers can constrain individual ordering or move the group together. Release the group first when needed to rearrange its contents.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-delete.text:
### 33 Delete

Delete removes instantly; the toolbar button adds an animation. Undo brings an item back if you go too far.

tool-detail-delete.text:
### 33 Delete — a closer look

#### How to use it
Use Delete for instant removal, or the toolbar dropdown to choose an animated effect. Multiple selected items can disappear one after another. Undo restores them.

#### Keep in mind
Deleting organizing tools such as clips, Clear Folders or rulers releases their contents rather than deleting those contents. Check the selection first.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-undo.text:
### 34 Undo / Redo

Step backward or forward through changes made by you and your AI. Try an idea, then decide.

tool-detail-undo.text:
### 34 Undo / Redo — a closer look

#### How to use it
Undo and redo desk changes one step at a time. Human and AI edits share the same history, so you can experiment with arrangement and appearance.

#### Keep in mind
The Doodle editor has its own temporary Undo. Applying the drawing adds one desk-history step. Panning and zooming are separate from object-edit Undo.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-zoom.text:
### 35 Zoom / Fit / Center

Move between the whole desk and small details. Fit uses your selection, then AI pointing, then all items. Center returns to the origin.

tool-detail-zoom.text:
### 35 Zoom / Fit / Center — a closer look

#### How to use it
Use the wheel or zoom buttons. Pan with Space-drag or the middle mouse button. Fit prioritizes human selection, then AI pointing, then the whole desk.

#### Keep in mind
If you get lost, clear selection and fit all, or find an item in Objects. Center returns to the origin. Follow a wayfinder when you want to see the route as you travel.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

guide-sample-object-pin-zoom.description: Zoom / Fit / Center: Try the example

tool-intro-object-list.text:
### 36 Objects

Find what is on the desk. Filter by type to locate items off-screen or hidden behind something else.

tool-detail-object-list.text:
### 36 Objects — a closer look

#### How to use it
Open Objects and filter by type. Select an item, then use Properties or Fit selection to find it, even if it is off-screen or covered.

#### Keep in mind
An item still exists when a cutout hides all of it. Select it from Objects to inspect its settings. The list covers this desk, not the contents of other desks.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-properties.text:
### 37 Properties

Adjust position, dimensions, colors and more. Available controls depend on the selected item type.

tool-detail-properties.text:
### 37 Properties — a closer look

#### How to use it
Select an item to see its position, width, height, colors and text settings. Use numeric fields when mouse adjustment is awkward.

#### Keep in mind
Size means different things for different tools: the sheet for a Doodle, endpoints for a line, and series settings for a pin. Some controls are restricted inside groups.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-files.text:
### 38 Save / Load

Use SAVE, SAVE AS and LOAD for server-side desk files. Upload and Download also work without AI.

tool-detail-files.text:
### 38 Save / Load — a closer look

#### How to use it
SAVE and SAVE AS write desk files through the MCP server; LOAD reads them. You can also ask your AI to save or load a desk. Save first before switching.

#### Keep in mind
Upload and Download use your browser and work without AI. They are separate from choosing a server-side path. Cancel an unsaved-changes prompt to keep your current desk.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-pdf.text:
### 39 Open as PDF

Open the whole desk as a single-page PDF in another tab, including off-screen items. Save or print from the PDF viewer.

tool-detail-pdf.text:
### 39 Open as PDF — a closer look

#### How to use it
Choose File → Open as PDF. The export covers the whole desk regardless of zoom or scroll, without selection outlines or editing handles. Open as PNG is available below it.

#### Keep in mind
Save or print from your browser's PDF viewer. This makes one large page; it does not paginate onto A4 or provide a separate print-layout editor.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

guide-sample-object-pin-pdf.description: Open as PDF: Try the example

tool-intro-appearance.text:
### 40 Desk appearance

Choose wallpaper, background, title color and frame colors. Show origin axes to mark where the first card begins.

tool-detail-appearance.text:
### 40 Desk appearance — a closer look

#### How to use it
Open Desk appearance from the menu. Set wallpaper, background brightness and title color. Names and colors help distinguish multiple desks.

#### Keep in mind
Toggle and color the origin axes. Set grid display, color and pattern independently, plus grid and snapping intervals. Register an initial focus from selected content if you want a saved opening view.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-bell.text:
### 41 Bell / Short note

An experimental bell sends a short note or your selection to AI while it is waiting. Use it alongside chat.

tool-detail-bell.text:
### 41 Bell / Short note — a closer look

#### How to use it
Use the bell to notify your AI of selected items or a short message. It can signal that you have finished an action when the AI is waiting for the bell.

#### Keep in mind
It cannot always start an idle AI. Delivery and response depend on the agent and connection. Use normal chat for longer discussion or when a reply matters.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

guide-sample-object-pin-bell.description: Bell / Short note: Try the example

tool-intro-thinking.text:
### 42 Think alone

Pause AI edits and pointing while you work. You can keep using the desk, and AI can still read it.

tool-detail-thinking.text:
### 42 Think alone — a closer look

#### How to use it
Turn Think alone on to stop AI editing and pointing temporarily. Your own desk controls continue to work.

#### Keep in mind
This does not hide the desk or disconnect the AI: reading remains possible. Switch it off to resume joint editing.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

tool-intro-pages.text:
### 43 Browser edition

Pages runs in your browser without AI. Open or edit desk files, then download your work to keep it.

tool-detail-pages.text:
### 43 Browser edition — a closer look

#### How to use it
The static Pages edition needs no installation or AI connection. Upload a desk file, edit it and download it again. A desk URL can also open a publicly hosted file.

#### Keep in mind
AI collaboration and server-side SAVE / LOAD belong to the normal edition. Public-file loading depends on the host and browser access rules. There is no automatic saving.

Blue wayfinder: back to the overview.
Pin ① ▶: example ②. Pin ② ◀: back here.

Green wayfinder below: visit 44 Camera.

guide-sample-pages-heading.text: ### 43 From your browser to your desk

tool-detail-camera.text:
### 44 Camera — a closer look

#### How to use it
Press Camera next to Lock. Move or resize the temporary capture frame, then Copy and paste into another app. Selected objects provide the initial bounds; you can also start without a selection or reuse the last area.

#### Keep in mind
Selection frames and editing handles are excluded. Capture any rectangle, including part of a card or some empty desk space.

Wayfinder above: back to 43.
Pin ① ▶: example ②.

text-0cc36b55.text:
# Tabletop — a tour of the tools

A shared desk where you and your AI can think together.

## Start with the green sign above

The green sign above this card is a **wayfinder**. Select it, then press the play button that appears. Follow the line to “Try a closer view”, try the instructions there, then take the next green wayfinder to **01 Card**.

## Follow what interests you

Small cards near the center introduce each tool. Detailed explanations and examples sit farther out.

Green wayfinders lead to details; blue ones bring you back. Tools run clockwise from 01.

Travel keeps your current zoom. Click the desk to stop along the way.

guide-try-selection-fit.text:
## Try a closer view

Select this card, then press **Fit selection** at the bottom right.

The view zooms to fit the card, making it easier to read.

Select any card and use Fit selection for a closer look. To go somewhere else, press a wayfinder's round ▶.

When you are ready, press the green ▶ above this card to visit **01 Card**.

guide-welcome-message.text:
# Make this desk your own

### There is no single right way to use it.

**Spread out material. Arrange ideas. Connect them.**
Doodle, press a stamp, and play a little. Choose your own tools and places.

---

These examples show possibilities, not rules.
**You do not need to learn every tool or keep everything tidy.**
Try one thing that catches your eye.

Think on your own or talk it through with your AI. New uses are welcome, even if they look nothing like these examples.

## Let your thoughts and habits shape the desk.

We hope it grows into a place that feels like yours.

---

In the connected edition, try asking your AI:
**“Open a desk. Let's think together.”**

guide-sample-text-card.text:

guide-sample-preview-card.text:
# Make an idea easier to read

Write normally, with **important words in bold**.
Use *italics for a quieter aside*.

## Today's idea
- Put the thought on a card
- Separate topics with **headings**
- Place related things nearby
  - Keep open questions too
  - Move from ~~an old idea~~ to a new one

## Try it
1. Double-click this card
2. Change a few words or symbols
3. Hold **Preview** to check the result

> It need not be polished.
> Leave it ready for your next thought.

---

### Code works too
Inline code: `const idea = "try it first";`

```text
Notice → place it → think together
```

[Read the Markdown guide](https://commonmark.org/help/)

For a quick note or a longer explanation.

guide-sample-preview-note.text:
Double-click to edit, then hold Preview before applying.

Supported: headings, bold, italics, strikethrough, lists, quotes, code, rules and web links.

The references below explain basic Markdown. Not every feature in those guides is supported: tables, embedded images, HTML and Zenn extensions are not available.

text-fd73071d-b8f0-4dc6-b880-0db6faaa835.text:
# Start with a small request

## Just one thing first.

> Make a card called “Things to do today”.

> Make this card a little bigger.

> Connect these two cards with a line.

**Ask once and watch what changes.**
Let that suggest your next request.

---

## When you feel at home, try these.

> Split this text into cards by topic.

> Arrange these cards so they are easy to read. Connect related ones.

> Help me think through this system as a diagram.

> Can you turn this rough doodle into a cleaner diagram?

> Match the colors and text here. Stamp the important parts.

> I cannot explain it yet. Look at this desk and help me think.

---

**You do not need to memorize tool names or every control.**
Say what you want to do or what catches your attention. Shape it a little at a time with your AI.

## Next, on your own desk.

Together, from the first card.
